requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects (IPv4) on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_redirects=1. Executor wrote /etc/sysctl.d/60-icmp-redirect-hardening.conf setting accept_redirects=0 for all/default scopes, discovered and corrected a gap for the pre-existing enp1s0 interface (which sysctl --system did not retroactively override), applied live, and verified all/default/enp1s0 read 0 both before and after a full reboot with a changed boot_id (e625b9a5... -> b5417ee9...), with the persistent config file confirmed intact post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets (IPv4) on node1
requirements.summary: accept_source_route was already 0 at baseline for all/default/enp1s0/lo but was made explicit and persistent via the same sysctl.d config file, verified live and again after the reboot with a changed boot_id, confirming both the setting and its persistence mechanism survive a restart.

overall_summary: The executor correctly and persistently disabled IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance on node1 via a sysctl.d drop-in file, caught and fixed a real gap where the pre-existing enp1s0 interface wasn't covered by the all/default write, and directly demonstrated persistence across an actual reboot (distinct boot_id before/after, config file and live values intact afterward). This satisfies both the standard persistence-claim bar and the task's own explicit persistence requirement.
limitations: Loopback interface (lo) accept_redirects remained 1 throughout (visible in cmd-34b457cc3dd04ee7); this is inconsequential for ICMP redirect security since redirects do not apply to loopback traffic, but is noted for completeness.

No independent traffic-level test (e.g., actually sending a spoofed ICMP redirect or source-routed packet) was captured; verification relies on sysctl/proc state rather than observed network behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands (writing/appending the sysctl.d config, live sysctl -w, sysctl --system reload, and the reboot) each map directly to satisfying the persistence requirement or to bounded, well-justified verification of it (pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, and post-restart recovery check as called for by the restart-evidence protocol). The enp1s0-specific correction was a legitimate fix for a real gap discovered during verification, not an unrelated experiment. The only minor residue is /tmp/reboot.log left from the backgrounded reboot command (visible in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot); this is trivial, non-security-relevant, and did not affect the target configuration. No failed services, package-manager damage, or unsafe exposure resulted from the changes (failed-services and package-health remained clean before and after).
